lines.text: A speck started the Gold Rush.
On January 24, 1848, James Marshall was building a sawmill in California.
lines.say: On January twenty fourth, eighteen forty eight, James Marshall was building a sawmill in California.

lines.text: He spotted something shiny in the mill's water channel.
The find was a thin scale of gold, not a big nugget.
The story goes that he bit it to test the soft metal.
He later said it made his heart thump.
By December 1848, President Polk told Congress about the gold.
lines.say: By December eighteen forty eight, President Polk told Congress about the gold.
About eighty thousand gold seekers arrived in eighteen forty nine.

lines.text: Soon jewelers set gold bearing quartz into brooches and watch chains.
That first speck has belonged to the Smithsonian since 1861.
lines.say: That first speck has belonged to the Smithsonian since eighteen sixty one.

post.caption: On January 24, 1848, James Marshall was building a sawmill in California when he spotted something shiny in the mill's water channel. The find was a thin scale of gold, not a big nugget. The story goes that he bit it to test the soft metal, and he later said it made his heart thump. By December 1848, President Polk told Congress about the gold, and about 80,000 gold seekers arrived in 1849. Soon jewelers were setting gold bearing quartz into brooches and watch chains. That first speck has belonged to the Smithsonian since 1861.
